owners.start: TestDataIsolationFixture constructor creates a process-scoped data root.
owners.stop: xUnit calls IAsyncDisposable.DisposeAsync after the assembly test run.
owners.teardown: Delete the isolated root with bounded retries and emit the lifecycle marker. No ProcessExit handler is registered.

owners.start: AvaloniaTestApplication starts the official headless test session.
owners.stop: Avalonia xUnit isolation disposes the per-assembly session.
owners.teardown: The package cancels its dispatcher token, completes its work queue and awaits the dispatcher task.

owners.start: The xUnit executable owns test fixtures and test-created background work.
owners.stop: Tests and fixtures must dispose every created Host, timer, task and external process before returning.
owners.teardown: Assembly fixture cleanup completes before the process is allowed to exit.

owners.start: The benchmark fixture starts one named dispatcher thread.
owners.stop: DisposeAsync cancels the token and posts a wake-up.
owners.teardown: DisposeAsync performs a bounded join and fails explicitly if the thread does not exit.

owners.start: BenchmarkDotNet creates an isolated benchmark process.
owners.stop: Global cleanup and disposable fixtures stop runtime work.
owners.teardown: No process-wide event handler may substitute for fixture cleanup.

owners.start: DesktopApplication creates one Host and the Avalonia controlled lifetime starts it.
owners.stop: MainWindow or controlled lifetime requests one idempotent asynchronous shutdown.
owners.teardown: Cancel application work, stop the Host with a deadline, detach process-wide exception handlers, flush settings/logs and dispose every Host/log/single-instance owner even when an earlier disposal step fails.

owners.start: Generic Host starts the bootstrap service, runtime, transfer backend and bounded workers.
owners.stop: Host shutdown cancels each owner and waits for workers/backends.
owners.teardown: Cancel, wake channel waiters, await worker completion, recover durable task state and stop external processes.

owners.start: The Generic Host or Avalonia view lifetime creates desktop services.
owners.stop: DI disposal, navigation disposal or application shutdown releases them.
owners.teardown: Long-running work must accept cancellation and be awaited by its owner.

owners.start: LoginCoordinator creates one isolated HTTP login session when a QR code is requested.
owners.stop: A replacement QR request disposes the previous session, and Generic Host disposal disposes the singleton coordinator.
owners.teardown: Dispose the named-client instance exactly once; IHttpClientFactory owns the pooled handler lifetime and no login session owns a background thread or timer.

owners.start: DI creates the logging provider and retention worker.
owners.stop: Host disposal flushes and disposes the provider and worker.
owners.teardown: Cancel retention work, await it, flush the sink and release files.

owners.start: The Generic Host or explicit test scope creates infrastructure services.
owners.stop: The owning scope disposes them.
owners.teardown: Dispose HTTP, SQLite, logging and write-behind resources through their injected owner.

owners.start: The transfer backend starts the external aria2 process on demand.
owners.stop: Backend shutdown sends RPC shutdown and disposes the process.
owners.teardown: Cancellation and bounded process termination prevent orphaned aria2 children.

owners.owner: DownKyi.Core injected service or caller scope
owners.start: The caller creates compatibility services and media helpers.
owners.stop: The caller cancels and disposes owned resources.
owners.teardown: External process, stream and file owners must expose deterministic cleanup.

owners.start: The caller invokes an application use case.
owners.stop: Cancellation belongs to the current operation or application lifetime.
owners.teardown: Application contracts do not own process-wide resources.

owners.start: Callers create immutable domain values.
owners.stop: No runtime lifecycle is owned here.
owners.teardown: Domain code must not create threads, timers, Hosts or global handlers.

owners.start: Program delegates once to DesktopApplication.
owners.stop: Desktop application lifetime completes before Main returns.
owners.teardown: No second Host, thread or global lifecycle owner is permitted.

owners.start: StartAsync selects containment from platform facts, starts the inert supervisor and authorizes one target only after ownership is established.
owners.stop: WaitAsync or DisposeAsync activates the same completion owner, which responds to target exit, caller cancellation, deadline and lifetime close.
owners.teardown: The lease terminates only its containment, reaps its supervisor, proves tree quiescence, drains streams, closes resources within the caller-owned TransitionBudget and publishes one typed outcome.

owners.start: The internal host capability starts the target only after the lease protocol establishes containment and sends launch authorization.
owners.stop: Lease finalization or the owner-channel fail-safe asks the capability to finish the direct child path; the capability cannot publish lifecycle results.
owners.teardown: Direct-child wait, target stream forwarding and target disposal remain subordinate to the lease protocol and platform containment authority.

owners.start: The router creates immutable stateless backend instances and selects one from captured platform facts plus the caller's strength requirement.
owners.stop: The router owns no active process, task, timer or containment lifetime.
owners.teardown: All lifecycle operations stay on the selected lease/backend authority; the router performs no wait, termination, retry or cleanup.

owners.start: The codec and state validator use immutable serialization and frame-order metadata; they start no runtime work.
owners.stop: Protocol calls return to the lease or internal host without owning process lifetime.
owners.teardown: No process, containment, wait, clock or cleanup authority exists in this seam.

owners.start: The selected backend prepares one delegated cgroup and attaches the lease's inert supervisor before launch authorization.
owners.stop: The lease or its internal owner-loss fail-safe terminates only the attached cgroup and observes membership through the same authority.
owners.teardown: The backend deletes only its exact owned cgroup after authoritative quiescence or during bounded setup rollback; deletion failure remains typed cleanup evidence.

owners.start: The probe creates one collectible AssemblyLoadContext or, only for the forensics self-test, one bounded residual child.
owners.stop: The probe unloads the context; the lifecycle gate identifies and stops the synthetic residual tree.
owners.teardown: A retained context fails the load phase. Residual-child self-test cleanup matches PID and creation time, kills the synthetic tree and performs a bounded wait.
